mantras.anvaya: इति उक्त्वा सा चण्डविक्रमा भगवती चण्डिका (12.33: देवानां पश्यताम् एव तत्र एव अन्तरधीयत)।
mantras.anvaya_en: An absolutive phrase and the subject; the main verb follows in 12.33.
mantras.lit: Having said thus, she, the Blessed Caṇḍikā, fierce in valour,
mantras.tr: Having spoken thus, the Blessed Caṇḍikā, fierce in her valour,

comm.t: The half-verse that closes the Devī’s speech in the narrator’s voice and opens her disappearance. The pairing चण्डिका चण्डविक्रमा repeats the root of her name: she is caṇḍa, fierce, in name and in deed.
Lalitā Sahasranāma (Brahmāṇḍa Purāṇa) also has the name Caṇḍikā (name 755, चण्डिका) and Bhagavatī (name 279, भगवती). The two texts are distinct works that share a vocabulary of names.

samasa.literal: those from whom dread has gone out

samasa.sense: each god’s own function — Indra’s rule, Agni’s, Varuṇa’s and the rest, which Śumbha and Niśumbha had seized (5.2–4)
samasa.alt: Also स्वे अधिकाराः (karmadhāraya, स्व as adjective ‘own’); the sense is the same.

morph.note: अन्तर् behaves as a verbal prefix, so the augment a- stands after it: अन्तर्-अ-धीयत. The passive of √धा has the stem धीय- (ā → ī). ‘Was placed within’, i.e. ‘vanished’.

Genitive plural of the present participle पश्यत् (√दृश् takes the stem पश्य- in the present system). With देवानाम् it forms a genitive absolute: ‘the gods looking on’, i.e. ‘while the gods watched’ — a construction that often carries the sense ‘in spite of’, here only ‘before their eyes’.

mantras.anvaya: (सा भगवती चण्डिका) देवानां पश्यताम् एव तत्र एव अन्तरधीयत। ते अपि देवाः निरातङ्काः (सन्तः) यथा पुरा स्वाधिकारान् (12.34: … चक्रुः)।
mantras.anvaya_en: The first line gives the verb for the subject of 12.32. The second begins a new sentence whose verb, चक्रुः, comes in 12.34.
mantras.lit: vanished right there, even as the gods were looking on. Those gods too, free from dread, (exercised) their own offices as before —
mantras.tr: vanished then and there before the very eyes of the gods. And the gods, their dread gone, took up their own offices as of old,

comm.t: The Goddess disappears in the place where she appeared (तत्र एव), while the gods watch. The gods return to their own functions (स्वाधिकारान्), which Śumbha and Niśumbha had taken from them at the start of the third story (5.2–4). The war ends where it began.
The disappearance (अन्तरधीयत) is read as the counterpart of her ‘arising’ (उत्पन्ना, 1.66): she is not destroyed or removed, she withdraws, and comes forth again when called (12.36).
Variant: GRETIL and Freund read पश्यतां सर्वदेवानां (‘while all the gods looked on’) for the Gita Press पश्यतामेव देवानां. The sense is the same; the Gita Press reading is kept.

flags.uncertain: Variant reading (corrections.json): पश्यतां सर्वदेवानां in GRETIL and Freund against the Gita Press पश्यतामेव देवानां; status ‘Textual Verification Required’. The analysis follows the Gita Press text.

samasa.type: upapada tatpuruṣa (भुज् from √भुज् + क्विप्; its first member यज्ञभाग is a ṣaṣṭhī tatpuruṣa: यज्ञस्य भागः)
samasa.sense: the gods restored to their right to the offerings, which Śumbha had claimed for himself (5.2, 5.108)

samasa.literal: those whose enemies have been struck down
samasa.sense: the gods, rid of their foes

morph.note: Perfect of √कृ, third person plural: reduplicated च- (k → c) on the weak stem क्र- with -उः.
Locative absolute: शुम्भे निहते, ‘Śumbha having been slain’. The past participle of √हन् is हत (the nasal is lost before क्त).
Locative singular of the feminine root noun युध् ‘battle’, a consonant stem: युध् + इ.
Locative singular of a masculine u-stem: the ending -औ (रिपु → रिपौ).

mantras.anvaya: सर्वे (ते देवाः) विनिहतारयः यज्ञभागभुजः (सन्तः) यथा पुरा स्वाधिकारान् चक्रुः। देव्या युधि देवरिपौ शुम्भे निहते, … (12.35) … दैत्याः च शेषाः पातालम् आययुः।
mantras.anvaya_en: The first line finishes the sentence of 12.33b with its verb चक्रुः. The second line begins a new sentence: its subject दैत्याः, a chain of locative absolutes (शुम्भे निहते … निशुम्भे च …), and the verb आययुः in 12.35.
mantras.lit: all of them, enjoyers of sacrificial shares, their enemies slain, did (their offices). And the Daityas — Śumbha, the enemy of the gods, having been slain in battle by the Devī,
mantras.tr: all of them, their enemies destroyed, once more receiving their portions of the sacrifice. And when Śumbha, the gods’ enemy, had been slain by the Devī in battle,
mantras.tr_note: चक्रुः, ‘did’, has स्वाधिकारान् (12.33) as its object: ‘carried out their own offices’, rendered ‘took up their own offices’ in 12.33.

comm.t: The cosmic order is restored: each god holds his office again and receives his share of the sacrifice (यज्ञभाग), the right Śumbha had seized (5.2) and boasted of (5.108). The second line turns to the defeated: the Daityas, whose fate is told in 12.35.

The verse fulfils, almost word for word, the terms the Devī sent to Śumbha through Śiva as her messenger (8.26): ‘let Indra regain the three worlds, let the gods enjoy the oblations (हविर्भुजः); you go to Pātāla if you wish to live.’ The return of the sacrificial shares is the sign, in Purāṇic thought, that the world is in order again.

samasa.type: bahuvrīhi (its first member अतुल is itself a nañ-bahuvrīhi: न विद्यते तुला यस्य)

morph.note: Perfect of √या with आ: reduplicated य-, the root ā lost before -उः (य-य्-उः → ययुः). आ + ययुः → आययुः ‘they went (to)’.
Locative singular of an in-stem (विध्वंसिन्): -इनि. The suffix -इन् (णिनि) denotes habit: one whose nature is to destroy.
शेष ‘remainder’ used as an adjective: ‘the remaining ones’. With दैत्याः (12.34): the Daityas who survived.

mantras.anvaya: (देव्या युधि देवरिपौ शुम्भे निहते —) जगद्विध्वंसिनि महोग्रे अतुलविक्रमे तस्मिन् (निहते), महावीर्ये निशुम्भे च (निहते), शेषाः (दैत्याः) पातालम् आययुः।
mantras.anvaya_en: The locative absolutes begun in 12.34 continue: तस्मिन् resumes Śumbha with three epithets, and निशुम्भे च adds his brother (निहते is understood). The main clause is शेषाः (दैत्याः) पातालम् आययुः.
mantras.lit: — that destroyer of the world, very fierce, of matchless valour — and Niśumbha of great might (being slain), the remaining (Daityas) went to Pātāla.
mantras.tr: he, the world’s destroyer, fierce beyond measure and matchless in valour, and mighty Niśumbha too, the Daityas who were left went down to Pātāla.
mantras.tr_note: The English keeps the locative absolutes as one clause, ‘when Śumbha … had been slain (12.34) … he … and mighty Niśumbha too’. The order of deaths in the story (Niśumbha in chapter 9, Śumbha in chapter 10) is not the order of the verse.

comm.t: The surviving demons are not destroyed: they go to Pātāla, the netherworld. This is the alternative the Devī offered them before the battle, in the message carried by Śiva (8.26): ‘go to Pātāla, if you wish to live’. With 12.34 the terms of that message are carried out in full.
That the remnant survives in Pātāla is read as why the Goddess must come again (12.36; 11.54–55): adharma is driven back, not abolished.

Variant: GRETIL and Freund read जगद्विध्वंसके for जगद्विध्वंसिनि (the same meaning with the agent suffix -अक). The Gita Press reading gives the pāda a light sixth syllable (जगद्विध्वंसिनि तस्मिन्: …सि नि तस्…), the variant the more usual heavy one (…स के तस्…).

flags.uncertain: Variant reading (corrections.json): जगद्विध्वंसके in GRETIL and Freund against the Gita Press जगद्विध्वंसिनि; status ‘Textual Verification Required’. Metrically the variant gives the regular anuṣṭubh cadence (sixth syllable heavy), the Gita Press reading a light sixth syllable; the analysis follows the Gita Press text. Also: the three epithets of the first line are taken with तस्मिन् = Śumbha (resuming 12.34); grammatically they could also be read with निशुम्भे.

पुनर् has an original r; before the unvoiced p it stands as visarga (before a voiced sound it would be पुनर्).

morph.note: With a prefix the absolutive takes ल्यप् (-य) in place of क्त्वा: सम् + भू + य. ‘Having come into being’ — the manifestation, not a birth from a womb.
Ātmanepada present of √कृ (weak stem कुरु-). √कृ takes either pada; Purāṇic verse uses both without difference of sense: ‘she makes, effects’.

mantras.anvaya: भूप, एवं सा भगवती देवी नित्या अपि पुनः पुनः सम्भूय जगतः परिपालनं कुरुते।
mantras.anvaya_en: One sentence: subject with epithets, a concessive (नित्या अपि), the manner (पुनः पुनः सम्भूय), and verb with object.
mantras.lit: Thus that Blessed Goddess, though eternal, coming into being again and again, O king, carries out the protection of the world.
mantras.tr: In this way, O king, the Blessed Goddess, though she is eternal, comes forth again and again to protect the world.
mantras.tr_note: The absolutive सम्भूय and the finite verb कुरुते are rendered as ‘comes forth … to protect’.

comm.t: Medhas turns from the story to King Suratha (भूप) and states its lesson. It answers the paradox he set out at the beginning: she is eternal (नित्यैव सा, 1.64), yet is said to arise (सा नित्याप्यभिधीयते, 1.66). The same words return here: नित्या अपि … सम्भूय.

The verse joins the three caritas into one pattern: each time the world is threatened she appears, acts and withdraws — the pattern the Devī herself promised in 11.54–55 (‘whenever trouble born of the demons arises, then I shall descend’).
Lalitā Sahasranāma (Brahmāṇḍa Purāṇa) has Nityā as a name (name 136, नित्या). The two texts share the idea of a Goddess who is eternal and still manifests.
